title: Insured Plan of Care Payer Authorization Schedule
content:
**Insured Plan of Care — authorization terms by payer program.** Each Insured Plan of Care is billed under one payer program, and the payer program fixes whether the payer must approve visits in advance and how the authorization clock runs. The figures below are the terms of each payer program; the rules that apply them to a plan of care are stated in the authorization and visit-billing policies of the Insured Plan of Care.

## Meaning of each term

- **Prior authorization required** — whether the payer program requires an approved prior authorization before treatment visits beyond the exempt visits.
- **Exempt visits** — the number of visits, counting the initial evaluation, that may be rendered before an approved authorization is required; 0 where no prior authorization is required.
- **Evaluation draws an authorized visit** — whether the initial evaluation visit draws one visit from the authorized-visit count once an authorization is approved.
- **Extension lead days** — the latest point, in calendar days before the current authorization end date, by which an extension request must be submitted; 0 where no prior authorization is required.
- **Extension trigger** — the remaining authorized visits at or below which an extension request must be submitted; 0 where no prior authorization is required.
- **Retroactive window** — the calendar days after the visit date within which the payer accepts a retroactive authorization request; 0 means retroactive requests are not accepted.
- **Pending follow-up** — the business days after submission after which a still-pending authorization request is followed up with the payer; 0 where no prior authorization is required.
- **Peer-to-peer window** — the calendar days after an authorization denial within which the treating therapist may request a peer-to-peer review; 0 where no authorization is required.
- **Appeal window** — the calendar days after a denial within which a written appeal (a redetermination or reconsideration for the Medicare programs) may be filed.

## Requirement table

| Payer program | Prior authorization required | Exempt visits | Evaluation draws an authorized visit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Commercial PPO Plan of Care | No | 0 | No |
| Commercial High-Deductible Plan of Care | No | 0 | No |
| Commercial POS Plan of Care | Yes | 1 | No |
| Commercial HMO Plan of Care | Yes | 1 | No |
| Medicare Part B Plan of Care | No | 0 | No |
| Medicare Advantage Plan of Care | Yes | 1 | Yes |
| Medicaid Managed Care Plan of Care | Yes | 1 | Yes |

## Timing table

| Payer program | Extension lead days (calendar) | Extension trigger (visits remaining) | Retroactive window (calendar days) | Pending follow-up (business days) | Peer-to-peer window (calendar days) | Appeal window (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commercial PPO Plan of Care | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 180 |
| Commercial High-Deductible Plan of Care | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 180 |
| Commercial POS Plan of Care | 7 | 2 | 14 | 5 | 14 | 180 |
| Commercial HMO Plan of Care | 7 | 2 | 0 | 5 | 14 | 180 |
| Medicare Part B Plan of Care | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 120 |
| Medicare Advantage Plan of Care | 5 | 3 | 0 | 3 | 14 | 65 |
| Medicaid Managed Care Plan of Care | 10 | 3 | 30 | 10 | 10 | 60 |

## Reading the schedule

- Only two payer programs show a retroactive window above zero: the Commercial POS Plan of Care (14 calendar days) and the Medicaid Managed Care Plan of Care (30 calendar days). Every other program shows 0, which under the definition above means it accepts no retroactive request.
- The four programs that require prior authorization each allow one exempt visit, counting the initial evaluation.
- Every payer program shows an appeal window, including the programs that require no prior authorization; the windows run from 60 calendar days (Medicaid Managed Care) to 180 calendar days (the four commercial programs).
